title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding is a way to represent categorical variables as binary vectors. Each category is represented by a column, and a '1' in a column indicates the presence of that category for a given observation.

title: Analyzing the Design Matrix
text: Look at the columns from $$col_1$$ to $$col_5$$. Each row from $$0$$ to $$4$$ has exactly one '1' in these columns, indicating a unique category for each row. Rows $$5$$ and $$6$$ have all zeros, which might represent a baseline or missing category.

title: Counting Unique Categories
text: How many columns are used for the one-hot encoding of the categorical feature?

title: Interpreting Rows with All Zeros
text: Rows with all zeros in the one-hot encoded columns often represent an additional category that is not explicitly encoded. Consider this when counting the unique categories.

title: Total Unique Values
text: Including the category represented by all zeros, how many unique values does the categorical feature have?
